scope: Phase 7 global release review of the backend (release-review-api), whole history 38b56c8..HEAD in four module runs (sonnet)

findings.title: Format tip example is a deterministic function of the accepted answer and can leak the key before reveal
findings.reason: The tip example only changes when the fixed example 4827 is itself accepted; any key-independent fallback still reveals that bit (that the answer is near 4827), which is the information the computed example carries. Tips appear only on UNPARSEABLE input and cost nothing; accepted residual.

findings.title: SignInFailureAdvice is global and bypasses the message catalog for non-sign-in unreadable-body and media-type errors
findings.reason: The advice is ordered first but delegates every non-sign-in path to Spring's standard handler, which still answers application/problem+json (no 500, no driver text); module advices with assignableTypes answer their own controllers first. Titles not from the catalog only for media-type errors outside modules; cosmetic.

findings.title: No brute-force resistance on admin sign-in
findings.reason: The store spec excludes lockout and rate limiting ("No sign-in lockout", OQ-23, NFR-2 LAN only); same waiver as slice 2.

findings.title: Admin session cookie has no Secure flag and no absolute lifetime
findings.reason: The store spec excludes TLS (LAN only, NFR-2); the cookie cannot be Secure without TLS. 8 h idle expiry per spec; same waiver as slice 2.

findings.title: Source update/delete and task create don't take the content lock, leaving a grade-lock / reference race
findings.reason: Single admin authoring by hand (one person, one browser); the race needs two concurrent admin writes within one request. The FK still refuses a task for a deleted source (now a 409), and a grade mismatch is visible and fixable in the task editor. Taking ContentLock in SourceService/TaskService.create is a candidate for UAT if it ever shows.

findings.title: Any DataIntegrityViolationException is reported as 'content-conflict' 409
findings.resolution: ContentProblemAdvice maps SQLSTATE class 22 (data exception, e.g. NUL) to a 400 content-text-invalid problem, keeps class 23 (constraint) as 409, and logs the SQLSTATE only. Test: ContentAuthoringIT 'a NUL character in task text is a 400 problem...' (red in f7a7cfd).

findings.title: Served-content queries are N+1 and load every task with its JSON each time
findings.reason: Child data volume is one child's practice (hundreds of tasks); measured round-trips are within NFR-5 in the slice 7–9 real-stack smokes. Batch lookups are an optimisation, not a defect; no behaviour change at release.

findings.title: Served-content checks do N+1 task loads per request
findings.reason: Child data volume is one child's practice (hundreds of tasks); measured round-trips are within NFR-5 in the slice 7–9 real-stack smokes. Batch lookups are an optimisation, not a defect; no behaviour change at release.

findings.title: Source update/delete take no content lock, so they race with task creation
findings.reason: Single admin authoring by hand (one person, one browser); the race needs two concurrent admin writes within one request. The FK still refuses a task for a deleted source (now a 409), and a grade mismatch is visible and fixable in the task editor. Taking ContentLock in SourceService/TaskService.create is a candidate for UAT if it ever shows.

findings.title: Duplicated RFC 7807 advice code in the child and admin practice advices
findings.reason: Duplication between two advices of one module; both are covered by their ITs. A refactor at release would risk behaviour for no user-visible gain.

findings.title: NUL (\u0000) in a child report note or answer can reach Postgres and cause a raw 500
findings.resolution: PracticeReaders refuses U+0000 in answer strings and selected keys, ReportRules in the note: field problem nul-character, 400, nothing stored. Test: PracticeIT 'a NUL character in an answer or a report note is a 400 problem...' (red in f7a7cfd).

findings.title: Unthrottled child problem-report inserts: no rate limit or cap on rows per task
findings.reason: Child endpoints are login-free by design on a LAN-only stack (NFR-2, OQ-23 excludes rate limiting); every report is legitimate feedback the admin dismisses in the flag queue (FR-41). A dedupe would change the FR-41 contract (each report is its own item); left for UAT.

findings.title: Checklist areas reviewed in the practice module with no defect found
findings.reason: Not a defect: the reviewer's own clean-area checklist (no finding).

findings.title: Client-supplied answer keys are echoed in problem `errors[].field`
findings.reason: The echoed field is the requester's own JSON property name, returned only to that requester; no stored value or third party is involved. Keys are bounded by the 16 KB body limit.

findings.title: Unauthenticated child report endpoint has no volume or attempt-count limit
findings.reason: Child endpoints are login-free by design on a LAN-only stack (NFR-2, OQ-23 excludes rate limiting); every report is legitimate feedback the admin dismisses in the flag queue (FR-41). A dedupe would change the FR-41 contract (each report is its own item); left for UAT.

findings.title: Login-free problem-report endpoint has no dedupe or rate limit, so the report queue can grow without bound
findings.reason: Child endpoints are login-free by design on a LAN-only stack (NFR-2, OQ-23 excludes rate limiting); every report is legitimate feedback the admin dismisses in the flag queue (FR-41). A dedupe would change the FR-41 contract (each report is its own item); left for UAT.

findings.title: Statistics read the entire attempt and hint history on every request
findings.reason: Child data volume is one child's practice (hundreds of tasks); measured round-trips are within NFR-5 in the slice 7–9 real-stack smokes. Batch lookups are an optimisation, not a defect; no behaviour change at release.

findings.title: Mission summary first-try count ignores tasks first resolved through another mission
findings.reason: Intended semantics (FR-32): the practice-flow store spec scenario Shared task earns nothing on the summary counts 9 first tries when task T was resolved in another mission, which is exactly the missionId filter.

findings.title: xp_award append-only trigger does not block TRUNCATE
findings.reason: Migrations are append-only and the app never issues TRUNCATE/UPDATE/DELETE on attempt, opened_hint or the ledgers (grep of src/main); the app role owns the tables, so a DB trigger is not a security boundary against it. Adding guards would also need the test cleanup redesigned (ITs TRUNCATE/DELETE between cases). Defence in depth only; not a release defect.

findings.title: Restore replaces the schema while the backend keeps serving and writing
findings.reason: Restore is an operator command run by the owner on an idle family stack (npm run restore -- --yes, owner-initiated); it takes a safety backup first and restarts the backend after a schema change. Stopping the backend around the swap is a sensible hardening for a later change, not a release blocker.

findings.title: NFR-2 bind guard is bypassable with plain `docker compose up`
findings.reason: NFR-2 is enforced by the documented start command npm run stack:up (guard + rendered-config check); the compose default is 127.0.0.1. Bypassing the documented command is an owner choice on their own laptop.

findings.title: Restore runs against a live backend with no write quiesce
findings.reason: Restore is an operator command run by the owner on an idle family stack (npm run restore -- --yes, owner-initiated); it takes a safety backup first and restarts the backend after a schema change. Stopping the backend around the swap is a sensible hardening for a later change, not a release blocker.

findings.title: Storage volume is not covered by backup although DB rows reference it by storage_key
findings.reason: NFR-10 asks for a Postgres backup command; files on doucko-storage are self-authored PDFs/images the admin can re-upload, and restore states explicitly that files are not restored. Volume archiving is a follow-up feature, not a defect of this release.

findings.title: pom 'no-sibling-contract' profile can silently skip codegen when ../docs is absent
findings.reason: Profile is inactive whenever contract/api/openapi.yaml exists (pinned submodule); CI and worktrees init the submodule, and a skipped codegen fails compilation anyway (controllers implement generated interfaces). Removal is cleanup for a later change.

findings.title: Tools address only project doucko-e2e; owner project guard verified (no defect)
findings.reason: Not a defect: the reviewer confirmed the e2e guard (no finding).

findings.title: Attempt log and problem reports are 'append-only' only by comment; no DB guard unlike xp_award
findings.reason: Migrations are append-only and the app never issues TRUNCATE/UPDATE/DELETE on attempt, opened_hint or the ledgers (grep of src/main); the app role owns the tables, so a DB trigger is not a security boundary against it. Adding guards would also need the test cleanup redesigned (ITs TRUNCATE/DELETE between cases). Defence in depth only; not a release defect.

findings.reason: NFR-10 asks for a Postgres backup command; files on doucko-storage are self-authored PDFs/images the admin can re-upload, and restore states explicitly that files are not restored. Volume archiving is a follow-up feature, not a defect of this release.

findings.title: Unpinned, floating base images and builder in Dockerfile and compose
findings.reason: Floating minor tags were chosen for security patches on a home laptop (ADR-0003 stack); reproducibility is not an MVP requirement. Pinning digests is a follow-up.

dispositionNote: Merged from four review-gate runs (a: admin/api/profile/shared/checking, b: content, c: practice, d: tools/resources/compose/pom); run c ended at its --max-total-usd 3.75 cap after all steps. An earlier opus whole-repo run (~$20) was stopped and left no record. 1 major fixed (red f7a7cfd, green aedd85f); 1 minor fixed in the same commit; the other minors waived with reasons.
